item.title: Opening Statement to the Standing Senate Committee on Banking, Commerce and the Economy

rating.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem testified before the Senate Banking Committee following a 25 basis point rate hike to 2.5%, the first increase since July 2023. The hike was driven by deteriorating inflation outlook stemming from elevated global oil prices and resilient economic growth despite US trade headwinds. CPI inflation is running around 3% and is projected to remain elevated through much of 2027 before returning to target by mid-2028.
rating.stance_rationale: The statement is moderately hawkish: the Bank has just resumed a tightening cycle after a pause, explicitly flagged upside inflation risks from energy prices and pass-through, and left the door open to further rate increases, while also signaling a cautious, meeting-by-meeting approach given elevated uncertainty.
key_quotes: There could be a need to raise the policy rate further, but given the uncertainties, we will proceed carefully.
With elevated inflation expected to last longer and the economy showing resilience, Governing Council agreed that risks to inflation had increased and there was less scope for monetary accommodation.
